claim.claim-text: 1. A method for verifying an integrity of event sequences of workflow events in a workflow system, the method comprising: logging each event of a set of event sequences associated with workflow events comprising one or more of:
(i) a workflow instance identifier for a workflow instance,
(ii) an event type,
(iii) a serialized event payload, and
2. The method of claim 1, wherein the event timestamp has microsecond-level precision.
3. The method of claim 1, wherein computing the respective rolling cryptographic digest is performed using a hardware security module (HSM).
4. The method of claim 3, wherein the HSM is Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 140-2 compliant and completes each digest operation in less than 2 milliseconds.
5. The method of claim 1, wherein the respective rolling cryptographic digest comprises a SHA-256 hash or equivalent cryptographic hash.
6. The method of claim 1, wherein verification by the recipient system occurs in under 10 milliseconds at a 95th percentile.

7. The method of claim 1, wherein the electronic message comprises a JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) or Financial Information Exchange (FIX) protocol message, and the embedded terminal digest is stored in a designated integrity field.
8. The method of claim 1, further comprising: retrying one or more steps of the method up to three times with exponential backoff in case of failure.
9. The method of claim 1, wherein the workflow system operates in a cloud-computing environment.
10. The method of claim 1, wherein the workflow events pertain to a financial transaction, and the embedded terminal digest is included in a regulatory reporting message.

11. The method of claim 1, wherein the workflow events comprise trade lifecycle events comprising one or more of: “TradeConfirmed,” “PaymentSettled,” and “DocumentAcknowledged,” each associated with a unique trade identifier.

12. The method of claim 1, wherein the workflow events comprise healthcare messages formatted in Health Level Seven (HL7) or Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) standards, and the terminal digest value is embedded in a metadata field or extension.
13. The method of claim 12, wherein the set of event sequences pertains to a financial transaction, and the embedded terminal digest is included in a regulatory reporting message.

14. The method of claim 12, wherein the set of event sequences pertains to trade lifecycle events comprising one or more of: “TradeConfirmed,” “PaymentSettled,” and “DocumentAcknowledged,” each associated with a unique trade identifier.

15. The method of claim 12, wherein the set of event sequences pertains to healthcare messages formatted in Health Level Seven (HL7) or Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) standards, and the terminal digest value is embedded in a metadata field or extension.
16. The method of claim 1, wherein the workflow instance identifier comprises a Medical Record Number (MRN) and an Encounter ID.

17. The method of claim 1, wherein the workflow events represent shipment events including “GoodsDispatched,” “CustomsCleared,” “InTransitScan,” and “ProofOfDelivery,” are associated with a Shipment ID.

18. The method of claim 1, wherein the terminal digest value is embedded in a metadata field of a shipping manifest or customs declaration in an electronic data interchange (EDI), eXtensible Markup Language (XML) or equivalent format.

19. A system for verifying an integrity of event sequences of workflow events in a workflow system, the system comprising: at least one processor; and a computer-readable storage medium storing instructions, which, when executed by the at least one processor, cause the at least one processor to be configured to: log each event of a set of event sequences associated with workflow events comprising one or more of:
(i) a workflow instance identifier for a workflow instance,
(ii) an event type,
(iii) a serialized event payload, and

20. A method comprising: receiving, from a computing device, an electronic message comprising an embedded terminal digest; and recomputing, for each event over a set of event sequences associated with workflow events, a respective rolling cryptographic digest from locally accessible data to obtain a result and comparing the result to the embedded terminal digest, wherein the embedded terminal digest is obtained on the computing device via steps comprising: logging each event of the set of event sequences associated with workflow events comprising one or more of:
(i) a workflow instance identifier for a workflow instance,
(ii) an event type,
(iii) a serialized event payload, and
